mil3.3.11:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of intention?”
mil3.3.11:1.2: “Intention, Great King, has the characteristic of intending and the characteristic of preparing.”
mil3.3.11:2.2: “Suppose, Great King, a certain man were to prepare poison and drink it himself, and give it to others to drink; he would suffer himself, and others too would suffer;
mil3.3.11:2.3: in the same way, Great King, a certain person here, having intended an unskillful deed with intention, when the body breaks up, after death, would be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
mil3.3.11:2.4: Those too who follow his example, when the body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
mil3.3.11:3.1: Or again, Great King, suppose a certain man were to prepare ghee, butter, oil, honey, and molasses together, and drink it himself, and give it to others to drink; he would be happy himself, and others too would be happy;
mil3.3.11:3.2: in the same way, Great King, a certain person here, having intended a skillful deed with intention, when the body breaks up, after death, is reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.
mil3.3.11:3.3: Those too who follow his example, when the body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.
mil3.3.11:3.4: That, Great King, is how intention has the characteristic of intending and the characteristic of preparing.”
